slides.0.title: Geography and climate
slides.0.subtitle: Latitude, mountains, lakes and sea in the Northwest and East Coast
slides.1.title: The Pacific Northwest: the Cascades rain shadow
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Latitude
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Washington's vineyards lie at about 45 to 47 degrees north, the same latitude band as Burgundy and Bordeaux
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The rain shadow
slides.1.highlights.1.content: The Cascades trap Pacific moisture: Seattle and Puget Sound get about 35 to 40 inches a year, while the inland Columbia Valley gets only about 6 to 12 (another source says 15 or less)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The Missoula Floods
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Floods about 15,000 years ago scoured the basin and left the sediments that now underlie the vineyards
slides.1.content: In one state, rainfall on either side of the mountains differs several-fold — the first step to understanding Washington.
slides.2.title: Continental conditions in the Columbia Valley
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Growing season
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A growing season of more than 150 days, over 2,000 degree days and 15 inches or less of rain a year; summers are long and dry
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Winter freeze
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Winters are cold, and deep winter freezes are the main threat
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Soils
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Windblown sand and silt (loess) over gravel and slackwater sediment on basaltic bedrock; well drained but low in nutrients
slides.2.content: The Columbia Valley is dry and sunny with winter freeze risk, so it needs irrigation and careful winter management.
slides.3.title: Oregon and the East Coast: mountains, lakes and sea
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Willamette Valley
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Between the Coast Range and the Cascades at about 45 degrees north, cooler and wetter than inland Washington
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Finger Lakes
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Deep glacier-cut lakes moderate temperatures and are the key to vineyard siting
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Long Island
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The Atlantic and the bays temper temperature extremes and lengthen the growing season
slides.3.content: The West is divided by mountains and the East is moderated by water — two quite different logics of coolness.
